title: Almond Butter and Jelly Sandwich on White Bread

content.title: About
content.content: The sandwich consists of two slices of white bread spread with almond butter and topped with sweet jelly. It is a quick, tasty, and nutritious snack that combines the healthy fats of almonds with the carbs of bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond butter is made from ground almonds and is rich in vitamins and healthy fats.
Jelly can be made from a variety of berries; strawberry, raspberry and apricot are the most common.
White bread is often used for sandwiches because of its soft texture and neutral flavor that doesn’t overpower other ingredients.
Almond butter and jelly sandwiches are popular among vegetarians and those avoiding dairy products.
The sweet‑tart combination provides a fast source of energy.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Almond butter contains a high amount of vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: The butter is a good source of monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Source of protein and fiber
items.content: Although the amount of almonds is modest, it adds plant protein and dietary fiber.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: White bread supplies quickly digestible carbs, useful before physical activity.

items.title: Berry antioxidants
items.content: Jelly made from berries contains antioxidants such as vitamin C and polyphenols that support immunity.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Almond butter can trigger allergic reactions in people with nut allergies.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Both almond butter and jelly add significant calories; portion control is advised.

items.title: Added sugar in jelly
items.content: Commercial jellies often contain added sugar, which may be undesirable for diabetics or low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: White bread contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread a generous layer of almond butter on one slice of bread, evenly top with jelly, and place the second slice on top. The sandwich can be cut into halves or quarters for easier handling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Store opened almond butter in the fridge and keep jelly in a cool place.
